verdict.rationale: cubic documents a versioned `cubic.yaml` at the repo root (or in an org-wide `cubic-config` repo) as the source of truth for AI review behavior, ignore patterns and custom agents, which covers the config file and path filtering. The docs do not show per-path instructions or selectable review profiles. Missing for 10: documented per-path instruction scoping, review profiles/strictness presets, a full config schema, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an engineering lead, I configure the reviewer with a versioned config file in my repo — path filters, per-path instructions, review profiles

citations.quote: `cubic.yaml` lives in the root of your repository and becomes the source of truth for AI review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, and custom agents.
Create a repository named `cubic-config` in your organization and add a `cubic.yaml` file to the root directory.
Custom agents are review rules that enforce your organization's specific best practices across pull requests.
